Class StackIteratorTest

java.lang.Object
myTest.StackIteratorTest
public class StackIteratorTest extends Object
Summary: This Test Suite verifies the behavior of the HIterator interface implemented by the StackAdapter's internal iterator. The suite is divided into sections using comments to group tests by the method being tested. Furthermore, it groups tests around sequential forward traversal and safe element removal, always ensuring full compatibility with the J2SE 1.4.2 collections framework.
  • Test Case Design: The tests have been developed following the Test Driven Development methodology, meaning they were implemented before their respective methods. The goal is to test sequential forward iteration, verifying the dynamic link with the backing stack and exception handling for illegal states (e.g., calling remove() without calling next(), or iterating past the end of the collection).

Conventions used in the documentation of the tests:

  • Every test starts from the same state: setUp() creates a new, empty StackAdapter (stackTest) before each test, so the Pre-Condition of every test is an empty stack and all the elements used are inserted by the test itself (as described in its Test Description).
  • The content of a stack is written from the bottom (index 0) to the top, e.g. [A, B] means that "A" was pushed first and "B" is on top. The iterators traverse the stack in the same order.

  • Method Details

    • setUp

      public void setUp()
      Creates a new, empty StackAdapter before each test, so that every test starts from the same known state.

    • reset

      public void reset()
      Releases the reference to the stack after each test.

    • testHasNextOnEmptyStack

      public void testHasNextOnEmptyStack()
      Summary: Verifies that hasNext() returns false on an HIterator obtained from an empty stack.
      • Test Case Design: Boundary case: iteration over a collection with zero elements.
      • Test Description: Obtains an HIterator with stackTest.iterator() without inserting any element and calls hasNext() once.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is still empty; the HIterator has not returned any element.
      • Expected Results: hasNext() returns false.

    • testHasNextStandardBehavior

      public void testHasNextStandardBehavior()
      Summary: Verifies that hasNext() reports correctly whether elements remain during a complete forward scan.
      • Test Case Design: Standard behavior of hasNext() checked before every step of a full traversal of a two-element stack.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A" and "B" (stack from bottom to top: [A, B]) and creates an HIterator. Asserts that hasNext() is true, calls next() (returns "A"), asserts that hasNext() is still true, calls next() again (returns "B") and finally asserts that hasNext() is false.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is unchanged ([A, B]); the HIterator is positioned after the last element.
      • Expected Results: hasNext() returns true, true and then false.

    • testHasNextMultipleCalls

      public void testHasNextMultipleCalls()
      Summary: Verifies that consecutive calls to hasNext() do not move the HIterator forward.
      • Test Case Design: Checks that hasNext() is a pure query with no side effects on the cursor position.
      • Test Description: Pushes the String "A", creates an HIterator and calls hasNext() three times in a row, asserting true each time. Then calls next() and asserts that it still returns "A", i.e. the cursor has not been advanced by hasNext().
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is unchanged ([A]); the HIterator is positioned after "A".
      • Expected Results: The three hasNext() calls return true; next() returns "A".

    • testNextOnEmptyStackThrowsNoSuchElementException

      public void testNextOnEmptyStackThrowsNoSuchElementException()
      Summary: Verifies that next() throws NoSuchElementException on an HIterator obtained from an empty stack.
      • Test Case Design: Exception handling: requesting an element when the iteration has no elements at all.
      • Test Description: Obtains an HIterator from the empty stack and calls next() once.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is still empty.
      • Expected Results: A java.util.NoSuchElementException is thrown by next().

    • testNextOnClearedStackThrowsNoSuchElementException

      public void testNextOnClearedStackThrowsNoSuchElementException()
      Summary: Verifies that next() throws NoSuchElementException once all the elements have already been returned.
      • Test Case Design: Exception handling: going past the end of a non-empty collection (the stack itself is not modified).
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A" and "B", creates an HIterator and calls next() twice, consuming both elements ("A" and then "B"). Then calls next() a third time.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is unchanged ([A, B]); the HIterator is positioned after the last element.
      • Expected Results: The first two calls return normally; the third call throws a java.util.NoSuchElementException.

    • testNextStandardBehavior

      public void testNextStandardBehavior()
      Summary: Verifies that next() returns the elements in the right order, from the bottom (index 0) to the top of the stack.
      • Test Case Design: Standard behavior of next(): correctness of the returned values and of the traversal order.
      • Test Description: Pushes the String "A" and then "B" ("A" is at index 0, "B" is on top), creates an HIterator and calls next() twice, comparing each returned value with the expected one.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is unchanged ([A, B]); the HIterator is positioned after the last element.
      • Expected Results: The first next() returns "A", the second returns "B".

    • testHIteratorRemoveOnEmptyIteratorThrowsIllegalStateException

      public void testHIteratorRemoveOnEmptyIteratorThrowsIllegalStateException()
      Summary: Verifies that remove() throws IllegalStateException when called on an HIterator of an empty stack before any next().
      • Test Case Design: Exception handling: remove() called when there is no element previously returned by next().
      • Test Description: Obtains an HIterator from the empty stack and immediately calls remove().
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is still empty.
      • Expected Results: A myAdapter.IllegalStateException is thrown.

    • testHIteratorRemoveOnPopulatedIteratorWithoutNextThrowsIllegalStateException

      public void testHIteratorRemoveOnPopulatedIteratorWithoutNextThrowsIllegalStateException()
      Summary: Verifies that remove() throws IllegalStateException when called on a non-empty stack before any next().
      • Test Case Design: Exception handling: remove() called without a previous next(), even though elements are available.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Integers 0, 1, ..., 19 (20 elements, 19 on top), creates an HIterator and immediately calls remove() without calling next().
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is unchanged: it still contains the 20 Integers 0..19 in insertion order.
      • Expected Results: A myAdapter.IllegalStateException is thrown and no element is removed.

    • testHIteratorRemoveDoubleThrowsIllegalStateException

      public void testHIteratorRemoveDoubleThrowsIllegalStateException()
      Summary: Verifies that calling remove() twice in a row, without a next() in between, throws IllegalStateException.
      • Test Case Design: Exception handling: each next() allows at most one remove().
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A" and "B", creates an HIterator, calls next() (returns "A") and remove() (removes "A", legal call). Then calls remove() a second time without calling next().
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: Only the first remove() has taken effect: the stack contains only "B".
      • Expected Results: The first remove() succeeds; the second throws a myAdapter.IllegalStateException.

    • testHIteratorRemoveDecreasesSize

      public void testHIteratorRemoveDecreasesSize()
      Summary: Verifies that a remove() on the HIterator decreases the size of the backing stack by one.
      • Test Case Design: Checks only the effect of remove() on size(), removing an element in the middle of the stack; which element is removed is checked by testHIteratorRemoveStandardBehavior().
      • Test Description: Pushes the Integers 1, 2 and 3 (stack [1, 2, 3], 3 on top), creates an HIterator, calls next() twice (returns 1 and then 2) and calls remove(), which removes 2 (index 1). Then reads stackTest.size().
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack contains two elements: [1, 3].
      • Expected Results: size() returns 2.

    • testHIteratorRemoveStandardBehavior

      public void testHIteratorRemoveStandardBehavior()
      Summary: Verifies that remove() deletes exactly the element returned by the last call to next().
      • Test Case Design: Checks the identity of the removed element: the element returned by next() (the bottom element, index 0) must be removed, while the other one (the top) must stay in the stack.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Integer 1 and then the Integer 2 (stack [1, 2], 2 on top). Creates an HIterator and calls next(), which returns 1, then calls remove(). Finally checks the remaining content with two queries: peek() and contains(1).
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack contains only the Integer 2.
      • Expected Results: peek() returns 2 (the top element is unchanged) and contains(1) returns false (1 has been removed).

    • testHIteratorRemoveTopElement

      public void testHIteratorRemoveTopElement()
      Summary: Verifies that remove() deletes the last element of the iteration, i.e. the top of the stack.
      • Test Case Design: Position coverage: removal at the end of the stack (the other tests remove at index 0 and in the middle).
      • Test Description: Pushes the Integers 1, 2 and 3 (stack [1, 2, 3], 3 on top), creates an HIterator and calls next() three times (returns 1, 2 and 3), then calls remove(). Finally checks size(), peek(), contains(3) and the HIterator's hasNext().
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack contains two elements: [1, 2]; the HIterator is at the end of the stack.
      • Expected Results: size() returns 2, peek() returns 2, contains(3) returns false and hasNext() returns false.

    • testHIteratorRemoveMiddleElementAndContinue

      public void testHIteratorRemoveMiddleElementAndContinue()
      Summary: Verifies that after a remove() in the middle of the stack the iteration continues from the following element.
      • Test Case Design: Cursor consistency after a removal: the element after the removed one must not be skipped.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A", "B" and "C", creates an HIterator, calls next() twice (checking it returns "A" and "B") and calls remove() (removes "B"). Then checks that next() returns "C" and that hasNext() is false; finally checks size(), get(0) and get(1).
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack contains two elements: [A, C]; the HIterator is at the end of the stack.
      • Expected Results: The next() after the removal returns "C", hasNext() returns false, size() returns 2, get(0) returns "A" and get(1) returns "C".

    • testHIteratorRemoveAllElements

      public void testHIteratorRemoveAllElements()
      Summary: Verifies that calling next() and remove() on every element empties the stack.
      • Test Case Design: Multiple consecutive removals: every element is removed, in every position, during a single forward scan.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A", "B" and "C", creates an HIterator and, while hasNext() is true, calls next() and remove(), counting the removals. Then checks the counter and isEmpty().
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is empty.
      • Expected Results: Exactly 3 removals are performed (no element is skipped) and isEmpty() returns true.

    • testHIteratorRemoveSeveralPositions

      public void testHIteratorRemoveSeveralPositions()
      Summary: Verifies that remove() works correctly when several non-adjacent elements are removed during the same scan.
      • Test Case Design: Multiple removals in different positions (bottom excluded, middle and top) within one iteration.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Integers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6, creates an HIterator and scans the whole stack calling remove() on every even value (2, 4 and 6). Then checks size() and get() at indices 0, 1 and 2.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack contains three elements: [1, 3, 5].
      • Expected Results: size() returns 3; get(0), get(1) and get(2) return 1, 3 and 5.

    • testHIteratorRemoveNullBetweenDuplicates

      public void testHIteratorRemoveNullBetweenDuplicates()
      Summary: Verifies that remove() deletes a null element and leaves equal elements around it untouched.
      • Test Case Design: Null handling and duplicates: the removal is by position, not by value.
      • Test Description: Pushes "A", null and "A", creates an HIterator, calls next() twice (returns "A" and null) and calls remove(). Then checks size(), contains(null), get(0) and get(1).
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack contains two elements: [A, A].
      • Expected Results: size() returns 2, contains(null) returns false, get(0) and get(1) both return "A".
